name: 42 QuakeHeroes
tagline: A U-Net deep network on decomposed seismic energy that finds the onset of moonquakes and marsquakes in noisy lander data.
problem: Planetary landers cannot afford the power to send continuous seismic data home, yet only a fraction of it contains quakes.
solution: A pipeline that band-pass filters Apollo and Mars InSight ground-velocity data, decomposes it with empirical mode decomposition, computes sliding-window energy per mode into a 2D matrix, and trains a U-Net encoder-decoder against Gaussian labels centred on each event's arrival time. A companion web page shows detected moonquake and marsquake types.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for the most innovative use of technology.
Used a deep neural network to locate seismic events precisely in time-series data, with advanced signal processing to isolate components of non-stationary signals.
Validated on held-out data: 63 lunar events for training, 13 for validation, and both available Mars cases used only to check that a Moon-trained model generalizes.
The write-up explains each step and why (filtering alone failed on low signal-to-noise, so they added decomposition), which makes the depth visible to expert judges.

lessons: For a technology award, show the pipeline and the reason for each step, not only the result.
State the validation split, especially when the target environment has almost no data.
LATAM precedent: a team from Brazil won Best Use of Technology.

sources.note: Team-written method, training and validation split, links to notebook repository and web page.
